tasks.title: cli: the argument parser and the two renderings

details.goal: One parser for both surfaces and one place that decides TOON vs JSON, so the CLI and the MCP answer cannot disagree about the bytes of an envelope.
details.contract:
Port src/shared/cli/args.ts (473 lines) and src/shared/cli/render.ts (60 lines).
Two parsers, both from the same field descriptors:
- tool calls, whose declared fields come from the seven manifests and whose undeclared keys are dropped (src/index.ts:1092-1106 shows the current behaviour);
- verb calls, which take their own flag set and REFUSE a flag that is not in it, with exit 2. The verb flag table is data in this module and must cover every flag the TypeScript CLI accepts today (src/index.ts:1399, 1440-1447, bin/sangkar.ts:60-90): worker takes --mode full|fast and --force; index adds --yes and --no-register; telemetry takes --out, --serve, --port, --host, --since; daemon takes a subcommand plus --port and --host (run only); repo takes a subcommand, a path, --watch, --watch-interval and --telemetry. Every verb also accepts the four globals.
Parser grammar, exactly: --k v and --k=v; --no-<bool> negation; a bare boolean flag means true; --k true|false accepted only for booleans; repeated array flags collect; integer-array items split on : (--range 1:5); a single positional binds the only required string field; a flag-prefixed token is never a value. Globals: --repo-root <path>, --data-dir <path>, --json, --help|-h; split_globals removes them and reports them, resolve_command finds the verb with globals on either side.
A wrong type, a missing required field, a refused key or a malformed value produces a usage error carrying that verb's or tool's usage block; usage_of renders the same block as the TypeScript side, including the clamp notes.
Renderer: render_json gives compact JSON plus a trailing newline; render_toon gives the encoder from TASK-010 plus a trailing newline; render_output picks between them; mcp_text gives the same without the trailing newline; exit_code_of returns 0 unless the status is Error or Bootstrapping (then 1). EXIT_FAILURE = 1, EXIT_USAGE = 2.
Tests: every case of tests/cli-args.test.ts and tests/cli-render.test.ts, plus one case per verb flag including --yes on index and its refusal on worker.
steps: Port the parser with the `InputLiteral`/`InputField` descriptors from the manifests (TASK-027..033 supply the data).
Port `usage_of` including the clamp annotations.
Wire the renderer to TASK-010's decided encoder and keep JSON byte-identical.
Write the tests, including one asserting `render_json` output equals `src/index.ts`'s `JSON.stringify(envelope)` for the same fixture.

Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test args_render` exit 0, 64 passed (e.g. the_json_rendering_of_the_status_golden_is_byte_identical, an_integer_array_flag_splits_on_the_colon_and_collects_repeats, yes_on_index_is_accepted_and_refused_on_worker, the_verb_usage_blocks_are_the_typescript_text). Deviations: (1) the seven manifests' input tables are verbatim FIXTURES in tests/args_render.rs because TASK-027..033 have not landed — each is replaced by the real table when its tool lands; descriptor types are the contract. (2) serde_toon 0.2.0's DECODER forwards deserialize_enum to deserialize_any, so it cannot read a unit-variant enum back (status: ok) — the tests therefore compare the decode against the JSON value (as tests/cli-render.test.ts does with decode()); the encoder is unaffected and nothing in the product decodes TOON. Orchestrator verification (independent runs): `cargo test -p sangkar-cli --test args_render` -> 64 passed, exit 0; workspace 461 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; clippy -D warnings and fmt --check clean. DEPENDENCY DECISION, mine to record because I authorised it: `sangkar-cli` gained `serde = "1.0"` and `serde_json = { version = "1.0", features = ["preserve_order"] }`. `docs/my-product/RUST-MIGRATION.md` §5 names `serde_toon_format` but not serde/serde_json explicitly, so a literal reading of "no new dependency beyond §5" would forbid the renderer from existing at all — but neither crate is new to the graph: `git diff rust/Cargo.lock` is +2 lines adding the two names to `sangkar-cli`'s dependency list, with ZERO new packages, and `sangkar-core` has carried both since TASK-001 (preserve_order is required for key-order parity). TASK-001's own contract says each crate "declares only what it actually uses", which is exactly this. Recorded so a later auditor does not read it as an unauthorised dependency. CONTRACT-TEXT CORRECTION: this task said `usage_of` renders the block "including the clamp notes"; I read `usageOf` in `src/shared/cli/args.ts` and it has no clamp annotations at all — the block is header, one line per field with `(required)` and the description, then the global-options line — and the clamp notes live in the verb blocks and the validation messages (`min`/`max` at args.ts:24-25 are read by the value check, not printed). The worker followed the TypeScript character for character, which is right; nothing was invented. TWO ITEMS FOR THE TOOL TASKS, the first of which is a byte-parity hazard: (1) an integral `f64` serialises as `0.0` under serde_json/ryu where `JSON.stringify` writes `0`, and `sangkar_domain::risk::RiskScore.score` IS an f64 (`round2(total.clamp(0.0,1.0))`), so a `summary` or `impact` payload with a zero or exactly-1.0 score will emit `{"score":0.0}` against the TypeScript's `{"score":0}`. TASK-028/TASK-030 must serialise the score so an integral value loses the `.0`, and TASK-036's golden harness must fail if it does not — this is not caught by any current test. (2) the seven tool `input` tables do not exist yet, so this task's parser is written against `InputLiteral`/`InputField` descriptors and the tests carry the seven manifests as verbatim fixtures; TASK-027..TASK-033 replace each fixture with the real manifest, which is the seam working as intended. Also noted, harmless: `serde_toon` 0.2.0's DECODER cannot read a unit enum back (`deserialize_enum` forwards to `deserialize_any`), so tests compare decodes against the JSON value the way `cli-render.test.ts` does; the product never decodes TOON, so only the encoder matters and TASK-010 proved it byte-identical.

details.goal: The trust tool: is the graph current, what does it cover, and what can it not see — with the repository identity and the health block.
details.contract:
Port `src/tools/status/manifest.ts` + `handler.ts` (602 lines).
Name `status`; description first sentence VERBATIM: `Report whether the graph is current and what it covers.`; parameters: `paths: array<string>` (default `[]`), `budget: integer` (default 800), `repo: string` (no default).
Payload top-level keys, in this order: `project{name,root,branch,remote,commit,db_path}`, `config{source:"project"|"global"}`, `graph{nodes,edges,size_bytes,db_path}`, `unresolved{total,material,buckets}`, `languages[]`, `paths[]`, `health{indexer,last_publish_ms,consecutive_failures,statement_cache_entries}`. `payload` is `null` for `bootstrapping` and `error`.

details.goal: Fetch more detail for one item from a previous answer: members, edges, source, coverage or outline — the tool an agent calls when a result was truncated on purpose.
details.contract:

Name `expand`; description first sentence VERBATIM: `Fetch more detail for one item from a previous result.`; parameters: `target: string` REQUIRED, `what: enum[members,edges,source,coverage,outline]`, `path: string`, `range: array<integer>`, `budget: integer` (default 2500), `repo: string`. Payload by `what`: `members{target,what,why,members[]}`, `edges{target,what,why,direction,depth,in[],out[]}`, `coverage{target,what,why,prefix,files[],not_indexed[]}`, `source{target,what,why,path,source_drift,window,content[]|null}`, `outline{target,what,why,path,members[]}`; plus `ambiguous{target,candidates[],candidates_total,candidates_shown,hint}` and `not_found{target,why,hint}`.

details.goal: The process entry point as bin/sangkar.ts is today: six reserved verbs, every other token a tool name, globals accepted on either side, usage on stderr with exit 2 — plus the fixed-order tool registry it dispatches to.

tasks.title: cli: the MCP server, route() post-conditions, in-band errors

details.goal: The stdio server: two handlers only, results framed as one text block, every error in-band, and the post-conditions the composition root applies to every envelope before it leaves.
details.contract:
Transport: the decision from TASK-011 (rmcp over newline-delimited JSON-RPC, or the hand-rolled frame). Server options: name `sangkar`, `server_version()`, capabilities `{tools:{}}`, and `instructions: INSTRUCTIONS_TEXT`.
Handlers: `tools/list` -> `[descriptor]` from TASK-034's registry; `tools/call` -> `CallToolResult { content: [{type:"text", text: mcp_text(envelope, output_json)}], is_error }` with NO `structuredContent`, `output_json` from the `--json` global, `is_error = status in {error, bootstrapping}`. An unknown tool, a bad argument, a cursor refusal, a budget refusal and a handler panic ALL become a text envelope with `status: error` — never a JSON-RPC error.
`route.rs` post-conditions, applied after every handler: `next_tools` is always replaced by `next_tools_for(tool)`; a `root_mismatch` staleness forces `read_status.stale = true` with its reason; `decisive = !stale`. A handler that throws becomes `fail(...)` built from `boundary_spec(store, tool, "<tool> could not answer", "the call failed before the graph answered")` with `UNKNOWN_COVERAGE {complete:false}` and an `unchecked_read_status`.
Shutdown: SIGINT/SIGTERM drain in-flight calls, then exit 0; stdin EOF is the client-gone signal. Nothing writes to stdout except the protocol.
Tests: replay `rust/tests/vectors/mcp_session.ndjson` and compare `tools/list` against the TypeScript descriptor JSON captured in `mcp_session_ts_only.json`; assert an invalid argument yields `isError: true` with a `cursor_invalid`-style envelope rather than a protocol error; assert a panicking handler yields code `internal`; assert stdout has exactly one JSON object per response and no other bytes.
steps: Wire the transport from TASK-011's decision with the two handlers.
Implement `route.rs`'s three post-conditions.
Implement the throw boundary and the two failure envelopes.
Wire signal handling and stdin EOF.
Write tests/mcp_surface.rs against the recorded session.

`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test mcp_surface` exits 0.
Done when: the replayed `tools/list` equals the TypeScript capture field by field, and a test asserts zero non-protocol bytes on stdout for a full session.

progress.detail: Transport wired: rmcp 3.11 `transport::stdio()` (DECISION.md's verdict), gated behind a new `features = ["transport-io"]` on the sangkar-cli rmcp dependency; the tuple of handles it hands over is the exact transport the spike measured. All three caveats from DECISION.md hold in this code: (a) responses arrive out of request order because rmcp spawns per-request tasks — `tests/mcp_surface.rs` keys every comparison by JSON-RPC `id` and a burst probe answered ids 1,6,2,3,4,5; (b) `inputSchema` member order survives because `sangkar-cli` keeps `serde_json/preserve_order` — the replayed `tools/list` is not only parsed-equal to `mcp_session_ts_only.json` but byte-identical when re-serialised; (c) rmcp never validates `arguments`, so refusal stays in `args::parse_args` and answers `CallToolResult::error` in band. Two handlers only: `list_tools` projects `sangkar_tools::registry::TOOLS[i].descriptor()` into `Tool{name,description,inputSchema}` (no rebuild, no derive), `call_tool` delegates to `mcp::Surface::call` -> `{content:[{type:"text",text:mcp_text(envelope,--json)}],isError}` with no `structuredContent`, `isError = status ∈ {error,bootstrapping}`; server options are name `sangkar`, `server_version()`, `capabilities{tools:{}}`, instructions. Every failure is in band: unknown tool (`not_found` + the seven names as hint), refused argument (recorded id-4 text reproduced byte-for-byte), refused repository, absent graph (`bootstrapping`, 5000 ms), refused cursor (`cursor_invalid` from the handler) and a handler panic all answer a text envelope, never a JSON-RPC error. `route.rs` owns the three post-conditions applied after every handler answer — `next_tools` replaced by `next_tools_for(tool)`, a `root_mismatch` forcing `read_status.stale=true` + its reason, `decisive = !stale` read from the final value — plus `boundary_spec`/`boundary_fail`/`UNKNOWN_COVERAGE{complete:false}`/`unchecked_read_status` for the two failure envelopes. The identity guard itself (`guardRoot`: recorded `project_root` equal = serve, recorded tree gone = serve with `root_mismatch`, other tree still present = `wrong_project_db` refusal) lives in `mcp.rs` because it is the composition root's, and it is what feeds route's second post-condition. Panic boundary: `std::panic::catch_unwind` inside `Surface::call`, wrapped by a hook swap that a drop guard restores and a process-wide mutex serialises (rmcp dispatches concurrently; a hook is global); the panic payload becomes an `internal` boundary envelope and the session keeps answering — proved by a test table publishing a panicking handler under a registered name. Shutdown: stdin EOF -> exit 0 (`ServerInitializeError::ConnectionClosed` is also 0), SIGINT/SIGTERM -> signal logged, an `Arc<RwLock<()>>` drain gate takes the write side so no new call starts and every in-flight call answers, then the service is cancelled and the process exits 0; the runtime is shut down with `shutdown_background()` because `tokio::io::stdin()`'s blocking read is parked on a pipe the client still holds and a plain drop would wait on it forever (this hung the binary until fixed). I did NOT add `Store::reader_handle()`: this surface opens the published graph per call (`open_store` + the identity guard) instead of pooling and refreshing, so a publish between two calls is read by the next call by construction — asserted end-to-end by `a_publish_between_two_calls_is_answered_by_the_new_generation`. Deviations recorded: (1) `main.rs` no longer holds `Stdin`/`Stdout`/`Stderr` locks for the whole run — a held `StdoutLock`/`StdinLock` deadlocks the server's own tokio stdio handles on other threads (it deadlocked on the very first run); stdin is now a `BufReader<Stdin>` (unlocked, buffered) and the outputs are plain handles, flushed before `process::exit`. (2) `get_info().instructions` is `INSTRUCTIONS_TEXT.trim_end()`, because the TypeScript publishes the guide with its file newline trimmed (4074 vs 4075 chars) and the recorded `initialize` frame is the oracle; without the trim the handshake differs by one byte. (3) `sangkar mcp <anything>` is now a usage refusal (exit 2, stderr block, no stdout); the TypeScript silently ignored leftover tokens — refused instead, because every other implemented verb refuses and a silently ignored `--mode fast` is a footgun. The worker checked the source and implemented what exists. tasks.title: cli: store lifecycle — fingerprint, reopen after publish, schema_too_new

details.goal: A server process must notice that a publish renamed a new inode over graph.db and serve the new generation — the behaviour tests/store-refresh.test.ts encodes and the one every stale-payload bug comes from losing.
steps: Port `fingerprint_of` through `std::fs::metadata` (inode via `MetadataExt` on unix, a documented fallback elsewhere).
Port `same_file` and its inode comment.
Port `open_store` and `refresh_store` including the schema_too_new refusal and the size read.
Write the tests, including a real rename-over publish.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test store_refresh` exits 0.
Done when: the rename case makes the reader answer the new generation id, and the unchanged case is asserted with a generous bound so it cannot flake.

progress.detail: Added the crate's library target so an integration test can link the module tree: `rust/crates/sangkar-cli/Cargo.toml` now carries a `[lib] name = "sangkar_cli" / path = "src/lib.rs"` table above the unchanged `[[bin]] name = "sangkar" / path = "src/main.rs"`, and the new `src/lib.rs` declares `pub mod args, dispatch, index_gate, mcp, render, repo, store_lifecycle` with crate docs saying why the tree lives there. `src/main.rs` lost its seven `mod` declarations and is now a documented `fn main() {}` shell over the library, so no module compiles twice and the code the test links is the code the binary runs. Filled `src/store_lifecycle.rs`: `FileFingerprint{path,inode,size,mtime_ns}` from one `std::fs::metadata` (`MetadataExt::ino()` under `cfg(unix)`, documented `0` fallback elsewhere; `mtime_ns` = seconds*1e9+nanos via `SystemTime`, negative before the epoch), `fingerprint_of` returning `Ok(None)` for NotFound/PermissionDenied and `AppError::internal` otherwise; `same_file` compares inode+size+mtime_ns and never the path (comment carried over: the publish replaces the inode, a path comparison *is* the stale-payload bug). `open_store(data_dir)` = `data_dir/graph.db`, fingerprint taken before `open_reader`, zero-byte file and absent file both `StoreFailure::Missing`, `meta.schema_version > migrations::schema_version()` → `SchemaTooNew{found,built}` with the handle closed; `db_size_bytes` is that open-time fingerprint size (never a live stat). Reconciliation of the two error contracts: `StoreFailure` stays the three-way lifecycle decision (plus `RefreshOutcome`) and exposes `code()` → `sangkar_core::errors::ErrorCode` (BOOTSTRAPPING / SCHEMA_TOO_NEW / INTERNAL) and `error()` → `Option<AppError>` (None for Missing; the refusal carries the TS message plus a hint naming the indexer's schema version). `refresh_store(&mut Store)`: one `metadata` on the recorded path, `same_file` → Unchanged; no file → Missing (handle keeps its generation); a different print → `open_publication` and, on success, one `*store = replacement` assignment swapping reader/schema/size together (old handle closed by drop) → Reopened; a generation that cannot be served (newer schema, torn file) leaves the previous reader and reports Unchanged — the enum has no fourth variant and `Store` carries no stale_reason per the contract, so the caller's disclosure belongs to the status task. Tests in `tests/store_refresh.rs` drive the real `with_stage`/`begin_write`/`migrate`/rename protocol in temp dirs (never this repo's `.sangkar/graph.db`): the publish test asserts the inode changed, the padded second generation is larger, the path stayed the same, and after `Reopened` `meta_for().generation` is g-b00002 with `db_size_bytes()` now the new file's size; the unchanged case asserts `Unchanged`, pointer identity of `store.reader()` (a non-flaky "no second handle") and a generous `elapsed < 25 ms` DoS bound (stat+compare is µs; a scan-or-reopen fails it); deleted → `Missing` with the generation still readable; bumped `schema_version` → `StoreFailure::SchemaTooNew{3,2}`, `code() == "schema_too_new"` and a hint containing `v2`, plus a rename-over too-new publish that refresh leaves as `Unchanged` serving g-c00003; absent → `bootstrapping` with `error() == None` and no file created; two 4096-byte files → same size, different inode, `!same_file`; and same path with a different inode → `!same_file` while a re-spelled path with the same inode → `same_file`. Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test store_refresh` exit 0, 8 passed / 0 failed — a_publish_renames_a_new_inode_over_the_live_path_and_the_refresh_serves_it, an_untouched_file_is_unchanged_within_a_generous_bound_and_keeps_its_reader, a_deleted_file_reports_missing_and_the_handle_keeps_its_generation, a_graph_written_by_a_newer_build_is_refused_with_schema_too_new, a_newer_generation_that_cannot_be_served_leaves_the_previous_reader_in_place, a_missing_database_is_a_bootstrapping_answer_not_an_error, two_files_of_the_same_size_are_not_the_same_file, same_file_compares_the_inode_and_never_the_path. `cargo test --workspace` 396 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (39 suites), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` exit 0 with no warnings, `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 0, `cargo test -p sangkar-boundary` 8 passed (stdout and DAG scans unaffected).

Orchestrator verification (independent runs): `cargo test -p sangkar-cli --test store_refresh` -> 9 passed, 0 failed (8 from the worker plus the one I added); workspace 397 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` zero warnings; `cargo fmt --check` exit 0; the `sangkar` bin still builds and runs (exit 0); and `sangkar-boundary` is green at 8 tests scanning 9 manifests / 21 edges / 117 source files with 0 violations, so the new `[lib]` target did not disturb the DAG gate. The restructure is right: `src/lib.rs` declares the seven modules and `src/main.rs` is a documented shell whose comment says a second declaration would compile every module twice and leave the code under test not being the code the binary runs. Manifest additions are exactly `[lib] name = "sangkar_cli" path = "src/lib.rs"` above the unchanged `[[bin]]`; no dependency added. Done-when satisfied: the rename case asserts the inode changed, the path did not, and the reader now reports `g-b00002`; the unchanged case is bounded generously (25 ms) so it cannot flake while still catching a refresh that re-opened the world. ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION, because the worker's own note called it a contract choice when it was actually a lost behaviour: `refresh_store`'s failed-reopen path returned plain `RefreshOutcome::Unchanged` with no log and no marker. `src/index.ts`'s `refreshStore` catch branch does two things there — it logs `store.refresh_failed` and it returns the old store carrying `staleReason: "a newer generation could not be opened"` — and the probe that matters is that `read_status.stale_reason` is a wire field in the parity bar. Reporting "nothing changed" while a newer generation sits on disk is the silent-staleness failure this task's own Goal line names as where every stale-payload bug comes from, so I fixed it rather than recording it: `Store` gained `stale_reason: Option<String>` with a `stale_reason()` accessor, the failure path now logs `store.refresh_failed` (reason in the message, since `sangkar-cli` has no `serde_json` for a structured field — log wording may differ, the disclosed fact may not) and stamps the reason, and a served replacement clears it because `*store = replacement` swaps the whole handle. Two tests pin it: I extended `a_newer_generation_that_cannot_be_served_leaves_the_previous_reader_in_place` to require the disclosure and that it names the version it found (`SchemaTooNew { found: 3, built: 2 }`), and added `a_disclosure_is_cleared_once_a_later_publish_is_actually_served` which forces the failure, restores a servable file, refreshes to `Reopened`, and asserts the marker is gone — because a marker that outlived its cause would be its own lie. The enum stays the contract's three variants; the second `Unchanged` case is additionally treated as `Missing`-shaped for a zero-byte stage (`open_publication` refuses it), which matches what a stage that never got renamed in deserves. NOTE for the status task (TASK-027): `Store::stale_reason()` is now the source for `read_status.stale_reason` when a publish could not be served; it is distinct from `sangkar_domain::freshness`'s five-value STALE_REASONS enum, exactly as the two fields are distinct in the TypeScript.

details.goal: sangkar repo add|remove|list|config must keep working: it is how a user registers the trees the daemon then watches.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/cli/repo.ts` (332 lines).
Subcommands: `add <path>`, `remove <path>`, `list`, `config <path> [--watch t|f] [--watch-interval ms] [--telemetry t|f]`.
Rules: `~/` is expanded; a positional that starts with a flag dash is refused (the first non-flag token is the path, `repo.ts:16`); `--watch-interval` outside 1000..=300000 is a usage refusal with exit 2; `config` resolves the tree the same way a tool call does (a named path, else cwd autodetection) and writes `<dataDir>/config.json` through `sangkar_core::repo_config`, reporting the file it wrote; `add`/`remove` go through `sangkar_core::registry` and are idempotent.

Port add/remove/list over the registry module.
Port config over the repo-config module, including the clamp refusals.
Port the stdout lines and exit codes.
Write the tests over a temp home and temp trees.

`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-cli --test repo_cmd` exits 0.

`/`already registered

`/`removed

`/`not registered

` (exit 1) and for config `watch=on|off`, `interval=ms`, `telemetry=on|off`, re-read after `repo_config::write_repo_config` so the file is the contract. `--watch-interval` outside `repo_config::WATCH_INTERVAL_{MIN,MAX}_MS` is refused at exit 2 before any write (`--watch-interval must be 1000..300000 ms, not 999`); the numbers are read from the constants. `list --json` prints `serde_json::json!({"version": REGISTRY_VERSION, "repos": ..})` + newline, and `tests/repo_cmd.rs` pins it byte-for-byte to the body `registry::write_registry` writes (core's `RegistryFile` is private and `Registry` is not `Serialize`), so key order/framing cannot drift. The workspace suite is not green: 3 failures in sangkar-tools/tests/impact.rs belong to a concurrent worker, not this task.

Orchestrator verification (independent runs): `cargo test -p sangkar-cli --test repo_cmd` -> 16 passed, 0 failed; `-p sangkar-cli` 111 passed; `cargo clippy -p sangkar-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p sangkar-boundary` 8 passed.
